meta.titre: Verb Conjugation: matching the verb form to its subject
meta.sous_theme: Choosing the correct personal ending of the verb

sections.contenu_markdown: In a class in Bamenda the teacher reads a sentence and the pupils must say how the verb ends. The sound is often the same for il parle and ils parlent, but the spelling is not, and the examiner marks the spelling. Many Paper 1 blanks ask only for the right form of a verb that you already know. If you follow a fixed method, you will not lose marks on these questions, and you will write better in Paper 2.

items: The subject pronouns are je, tu, il/elle, nous, vous, ils/elles.
The infinitive of a regular verb ends in -er, -ir or -re.
A verb must agree in person and number with its subject.

sections.titre: Method and forms for conjugation gaps
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Method for any conjugation gap

1. Find the real subject: the noun or pronoun the verb refers to, not the nearest noun.
2. Replace the subject with a pronoun (*Les élèves* = *ils*).
3. Find the tense from the time clues.
4. Take the infinitive and write the ending that goes with that pronoun.

### Present tense of the verbs the examination likes

| | être | avoir | aller | faire | pouvoir | vouloir |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| je | suis | ai | vais | fais | peux | veux |
| tu | es | as | vas | fais | peux | veux |
| il / elle | est | a | va | fait | peut | veut |
| nous | sommes | avons | allons | faisons | pouvons | voulons |
| vous | êtes | avez | allez | faites | pouvez | voulez |
| ils / elles | sont | ont | vont | font | peuvent | veulent |

### Regular endings in the present

| | -er (*parler*) | -ir (*finir*) | -re (*vendre*) |
|---|---|---|---|
| je | parle | finis | vends |
| tu | parles | finis | vends |
| il / elle | parle | finit | vend |
| nous | parlons | finissons | vendons |
| vous | parlez | finissez | vendez |
| ils / elles | parlent | finissent | vendent |

The ending *-ent* of ils and elles is silent in -er verbs, but it must be written. Do not confuse *ont* (avoir) with *on*, nor *sont* (être) with *son* (his or her).

### Other tenses in one line

Imparfait: the stem of *nous* in the présent + *-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient* (*nous chantons* → *je chantais*; être is irregular: *j'étais*). Futur simple: infinitive + *-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont* (*nous parlerons*; *vendre* drops its final e: *je vendrai*). Passé composé: avoir or être in the présent + past participle.

variantes.nom: The subject is not next to the verb
variantes.quand_utiliser: When words come between the subject and the verb, or the subject follows the verb
variantes.contenu_markdown: Ignore the words between the subject and the verb. *Les élèves de ma classe, qui adorent le football, jouent chaque samedi.* (The pupils in my class, who love football, play every Saturday.) The subject is *les élèves* (ils), so the verb is *jouent*. In a question the subject may follow the verb: *Où vont tes frères ?* (Where are your brothers going?) The subject is *tes frères* (ils), so the verb is *vont*.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the verb is manger, commencer, appeler, acheter or préférer
variantes.contenu_markdown: *Manger* keeps an e before -ons: *nous mangeons*. *Commencer* takes a cedilla: *nous commençons*. *Appeler* doubles the l: *j'appelle*, *ils appellent*, but *nous appelons*. *Acheter* takes a grave accent: *j'achète*, *ils achètent*, but *nous achetons*. *Préférer* gives *je préfère*, *nous préférons*.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the verb is in the passé composé
variantes.contenu_markdown: Most verbs use avoir: *Tu as pris le bus.* (You took the bus.) Aller, venir, arriver, partir, entrer, sortir, rester, tomber, naître, mourir and all reflexive verbs use être, and the participle then agrees with the subject: *Elle est partie.* (She left.) *Nous nous sommes levés tôt.* (We got up early.) Learn the common irregular participles: faire → fait; prendre → pris; voir → vu; avoir → eu; être → été; écrire → écrit; dire → dit; venir → venu; pouvoir → pu; vouloir → voulu.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Les marchands du quartier ____ leurs produits très tôt le matin.
A) vend   B) vendent   C) vendons   D) vendez

etapes.justification: The subject is *Les marchands*. *Du quartier* only tells which traders, and the singular noun quartier must not decide the ending.
Nothing points to the past or to the future; the sentence describes what traders do, so it is in the présent.

etapes.action: Write the form of the verb.
etapes.justification: The infinitive is vendre, a regular -re verb. Its forms are vends, vends, vend, vendons, vendez, vendent.
Vend goes with il, vendons with nous and vendez with vous.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The answer is **B) vendent**. The sentence means: 'The traders of the neighbourhood sell their goods very early in the morning.'

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: *Les enfants joue dans la cour.* (incorrect)
items.pourquoi_faux: The subject *les enfants* is plural (ils), so the verb must end in -ent even though this ending is not pronounced.
items.correction_markdown: *Les enfants jouent dans la cour.* (The children play in the yard.)

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: *Vous faisez vos devoirs.* (incorrect)
items.pourquoi_faux: Faire is irregular: the form for vous is *faites*, not *faisez*.
items.correction_markdown: *Vous faites vos devoirs.* (You do your homework.)

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: *Mes amis son toujours à l'heure.* (incorrect)
items.pourquoi_faux: *Son* means 'his or her'. The verb être is needed, and the form for ils is *sont*.
items.correction_markdown: *Mes amis sont toujours à l'heure.* (My friends are always on time.)

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: *Nous mangons du riz.* (incorrect)
items.pourquoi_faux: Before -ons the verb manger keeps its e so that the g stays soft.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: *Elle a allé au marché.* (incorrect)
items.pourquoi_faux: Aller forms its passé composé with être, not with avoir, and the participle agrees with the subject.
items.correction_markdown: *Elle est allée au marché.* (She went to the market.)

items.enonce_markdown:
Tu ____ très bien le français.
A) parles   B) parle   C) parlons   D) parlent
items.solution_markdown: The subject is *tu*, and -er verbs end in -es with tu. Answer **A) parles**.

items.enonce_markdown:
Mes cousins et moi ____ au village chaque année.
A) vont   B) allez   C) allons   D) va
items.solution_markdown: *Mes cousins et moi* can be replaced by *nous*, so the verb is *allons*. Answer **C**. Vont goes with ils, allez with vous and va with il.

items.enonce_markdown:
Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
(a) Vous ne (faire) ____ jamais de bruit en classe.
(b) Les deux frères (pouvoir) ____ porter ce sac ensemble.
(c) Hier, Aïcha (aller) ____ au marché et (acheter) ____ du poisson.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) vous → **faites**.

(b) The subject *les deux frères* = ils, so **peuvent**.

(c) *Hier* needs the passé composé. Aller takes être and the participle agrees with Aïcha (a girl): **est allée**. Acheter takes avoir: **a acheté**.

items_markdown: Find the real subject, replace it with a pronoun, find the tense, then write the ending.
Learn the présent of être, avoir, aller, faire, pouvoir and vouloir by heart, especially vous faites, ils sont, ils ont, ils vont, ils font.
The ending -ent of ils and elles is silent in -er verbs but compulsory in writing; do not confuse ont/on and sont/son.
Some -er verbs change their spelling: nous mangeons, nous commençons, j'achète, j'appelle.
In the passé composé choose the auxiliary (avoir or être) first, then the participle; with être the participle agrees with the subject.
